triage.note: tagged invariant — a hand-maintained count is wrong again by the next milestone, and this repo has already burned a review round on three documents carrying three different totals for the same thing (PR #15, R19). The failure mode this closes is not the wrong number, it is the number that nothing recomputes. Adding a case to the suite now turns this red until README is updated, which is the intended cost. D8's cited reports are immutable artifacts, so its assertion is stable; moving the range means citing the runs it was measured from. The block cites report files rather than recomputing 'the latest run' on purpose: a report is immutable, so the assertion is stable, and moving the block means citing the runs it was measured from — the same contract D8's retired half had. The M29 half is the same shape one level up: a milestone's own ADR asserted its gate criterion was green-pending, and the milestone after it is the one that knows whether pending resolved true or false — nothing forced that resolution back into the ADR until this case checked for it. PR #28 R3 (LOW, routed to debt, tasks/TODO.md T-R33): prompts/ is append-only — a curated file records what was known and decided on its date and is never rewritten to look right in hindsight (the same principle ADR-015's own struck-not-deleted amendments follow, stated explicitly for prompts/ in prompts/README.md). prompts/014-a-freeze.md keeping its original 'green offline, pending' wording is correct by that convention, not a defect — a live reader who wants the current status reads specs/decisions/ADR-015-a-freeze.md, which this M29/M28 work keeps current, not a dated prompt record. PR #28 R4/R5: the markdown-strip ceiling is now literal and stated precisely (bold/italic/link unwrapped, underscore emphasis deliberately not — a real gap, named rather than implied), and the `prompts/` carve-out from R3 turned out to be the same mistake as the original 5-file allowlist one level down — excluding a directory is just a coarser allowlist. The general lesson, stated once rather than per-finding: for a guard whose job is 'does prose currently assert X', the safe move is to strike/fix the false claim, not to stop looking at the file that contains it.
